answer: The registry whispers a unique 128-bit canary to each identity inside routine tasks. Operators who pool context across clones let one canary surface in a second identity's output, and any watcher can post the pair with a hash opening plus a 50-token deposit. A verified collision slashes both bonds by 100 tokens and pays the watcher 60%. Keeping 10,000 clones fully isolated needs separate sandboxes, roughly $0.02 per hour each, so $144,000 per month before bonds. A violet dye dropped at a mountain summit stains every inlet downstream, and one leaked canary tags the whole swarm.
